answer: The contract contains a sample Non-Disclosure and Non-Competition Agreement in Appendix C, which restricts the Franchisee's personnel (Members) from engaging in competitive businesses. Specifically, during the term of the Franchise Agreement, Members are prohibited from owning, managing, or having any interest in a business that operates a restaurant featuring pizza or offers substantially similar products/services. Additionally, during a two-year Post-Term Period, Members are restricted from engaging in such competitive businesses within a three-mile radius of the Franchised Business.

evidence.text: 2. Covenants Not to Compete. (a) Member specifically acknowledges that, pursuant to the Franchise Agreement, and by virtue of its position with Franchisee, Member will receive valuable specialized training and Confidential Information, including, without limitation, information regarding the operational, sales, promotional, and marketing methods and techniques of Franchisor and the System. (b) Member covenants and agrees that during the term of the Franchise Agreement, except as otherwise approved in writing by Franchisor, Member shall not, either directly or indirectly, for itself, or through, on behalf of, or in conjunction with any person, persons, partnership, corporation, or entity: (i) Own, manage, engage in, be employed by, advise, make loans to, consult for, rent or lease to, or have any other interest in business that (directly or indirectly) operates, or grants franchises or licenses to operate, a restaurant featuring pizza and related food specialties or that offers products or services substantially similar to those then offered by Pizza Fusions Restaurants ("Competitive Business");

(c) Member covenants and agrees that during the Post-Term Period (defined below), except as otherwise approved in writing by Franchisor, Member shall not, either directly or indirectly, own, manage, engage in, be employed by, advise, make loans to, consult for, or have any other interest in any Competitive Business that is, or intends to operate, within a three (3) mile radius of the premises of your Franchised Business or within a three (3) mile radius of any Franchised Business then-operating or under construction to operate under the System. (d) As used in this Agreement, the term "Post-Term Period" shall mean a continuous uninterrupted period of two (2) years from the date of: (a) a transfer permitted under Section 14 of the Franchise Agreement; (b) expiration or termination of the Franchise Agreement (regardless of the cause for termination); (c) termination of Member's employment with Franchisee; and/or (d) a final order of a duly authorized arbitrator, panel of arbitrators, or a court of competent jurisdiction (after all appeals have been taken) with respect to any of the foregoing or with respect to the enforcement of this Agreement;

It also restricts the Member from owning, managing, or engaging in a Competitive Business within a three-mile radius of the Franchised Business during the Post-Term Period (two years after termination).

answer: The contract contains two specific 'Most Favoured Treatment' clauses. Section 4.02 applies to the Reseller Agreement, stating that terms shall be no less favorable to Nortel than those in effect with any of Entrust's other resellers at the time the agreement is executed. Section 5.02 applies to the Source Code License, stating that terms shall be no less favorable to Nortel than those in effect with any of Entrust's source code licensees receiving substantially similar rights, taking into account the relative size of the licensee and Entrust's potential benefits. The contract does not contain a clause requiring automatic adjustment if better terms are offered to third parties after the initial execution; rather, it sets a baseline comparison to existing third-party terms at the time of execution or current terms for source code licenses.

The contract contains significant exclusivity and competition restriction clauses. Section 1.2 imposes a non-compete obligation on the Distributor, prohibiting them from procuring, manufacturing, marketing, or selling any implantable medical devices that compete with STAAR's Products in the Territory during the term. Section 1.3 grants the Distributor an exclusive right to market, distribute, and sell the Products in the Territory, subject to Section 8.3. However, this exclusivity is qualified by Section 1.3, which reserves STAAR's right to sell Products directly (e.g., via e-commerce) without compensation to the Distributor, and Section 1.7, which allows STAAR to sell other products or Products on an OEM basis in the Territory. Additionally, Section 6.8 imposes a post-termination non-compete restriction: if the Distributor terminates the agreement, they are prohibited from selling or marketing competitive products in the Territory for one year thereafter.

answer: The contract establishes an exclusive distribution arrangement. The Company appoints the Distributor as the 'exclusive distributor' of Products within the defined Market (State of Illinois). The Distributor is granted the 'exclusive right to sell and distribute Products' in that territory. Additionally, the Distributor is obligated to purchase Products solely from the Company ('shall not order or purchase Products from any source other than the Company'). The exclusivity is conditional on the Distributor meeting minimum purchase expectations; failure to do so allows the Company to reevaluate the exclusive rights. The Distributor also has an option to become the exclusive distributor for new products introduced by the Company.

answer: The contract contains specific restrictions on PlanetCAD regarding the solicitation and marketing of services to Dassault Systemes Customers. During the term of the agreement and for one year thereafter, PlanetCAD is prohibited from marketing any services to Customers without Dassault Systemes' prior written approval. Additionally, PlanetCAD may only market new functions directly to Dassault Systemes Customers with prior written approval, unless the customer contact information was obtained from an independent source unrelated to the agreement and no data from the Dassault Systemes Customer Database was used. There are no corresponding no-solicit restrictions placed on Dassault Systemes regarding PlanetCAD's customers in this agreement.

answer: The contract contains an exclusive dealing commitment regarding the use of Peyton Manning's likeness for the specific product category (cold breakfast cereals) within the defined territory. Section 2(a) grants the Company the 'exclusive right and license' to use the Manning Identification for advertising and promotion of Products. Crucially, it states that Pey Dirt 'expressly agrees that the right to use Manning Identification will not be granted to anyone other than Company' for this purpose during the Contract Period. However, Section 24 clarifies that this exclusivity is limited to 'Products themselves' and does not prevent Pey Dirt from authorizing others to use the identification for other tangible and intangible items and services. Additionally, Section 4(e) includes a Most Favored Nation clause requiring the Company to match higher remuneration paid to other NFL quarterbacks for similar regional endorsements.
